taylor: Quick follow-up: after the RFC we need to settle on a deterministic fallback order when midstream handoffs fail. We saw a case where frontdoor retried to a cheaper model and got inconsistent partial outputs. Need safe defaults.

nina: Agreed. Proposal: fallback order priority list configured per-route: [primary, safe-variant, degraded-latency, fail]. Frontdoor tries each option in sequence if resume/restart can't complete.

alex: How do we detect 'can't complete'? timeouts, worker rejects resume, or resume validation fails (signature mismatch). Also consider soft degraded responses vs hard failures.

taylor: Yes. We'll classify outcomes: accept, reject-restart, reject-fallback, timeout. Only reject-fallback triggers next in priority list. timeout -> next only if deadline elapsed.

nina: Also, mandate an output wrapper: when serving from fallback, add X-Fallback-Used: true;X-Fallback-Reason: <code>. That helps customer support and quality monitoring.

alex: infra-bot: link to updated config schema?

infra-bot: Route schema draft: https://internal.rw/router-schema#fallback_policy (nina)

nina: Let's not allow cascading fallbacks more than 2 steps by default to bound latency. Configurable up to 4 for tolerant routes.

taylor: Ok. Action items: nina -> land route schema; alex -> implement fallback header and reason codes; taylor -> add integration test that simulates resume rejection and inspects chosen fallback and emitted headers.

infra-bot: Noted.
